answer_1.quote: The report labeling task is to extract the presence of one or more clinically important observations from a free-text radiology report.

answer_2.quote: Models are evaluated on their average performance on three retrieval tasks: positive extraction, negative extraction, and uncertainty extraction. For each of the tasks, the class of interest is treated as the positive class, and the other classes are considered negative. For each of the 14 observations, we compute a weighted average of the F1 scores on each of the above three tasks, weighted by the support for each class of interest, which we call the weighted-F1 metric, henceforth simply abbreviated to F1.

answer_3.quote: We introduce a method for radiology report labeling, in which a biomedically pretrained BERT model is first trained on annotations of a rule-based labeler, and then fine-tuned on a small set of expert annotations augmented with automated backtranslation.

answer_4.quote: the ground truth labels for the MIMIC-CXR test set were determined by a single board-certified radiologist
